thread.title: ‘Smart money’ signals are positive for only 2 of these 10 popular tech stocks

author: Nigam Arora
title: ‘Smart money’ signals are positive for only 2 of these 10 popular tech stocks
text:
Earnings on many popular tech stocks, including FAANG stocks, are out. For the most part, earnings are better than the consensus numbers but worse than the whisper numbers. 
Moreover, tech stocks have had a good run. How much of the good news is already discounted in the prices? Should you buy or sell? A helpful technique is to look at segmented money flows. 
The chart Please click here for a chart showing money flows in popular tech stocks. It shows money flows in FAANG stocks of Facebook FB, -0.48% , Apple AAPL, -2.44% Amazon AMZN, +5.31% Netflix NFLX, +0.83% and Alphabet GOOG, -4.09% GOOGL, -4.86% 
It also shows money flows in popular tech stocks of AMD AMD, -4.49% Alibaba BABA, -1.09% Microsoft MSFT, -1.39% Nvidia NVDA, -1.74% and Tesla TSLA, -0.68% 
Note the following:
• The “smart money flows” are positive only for Facebook and Alibaba. 
• Those flows are negative for AMD, Nvidia and Tesla. 
• They are neutral for Apple, Amazon, Netflix and Alphabet.
• The momo (momentum) crowd is aggressively buying tech stocks.
• Short squeezes are adding to the buying. In a short squeeze, short sellers panic and buy to cover to cut their losses. This adds fuel to the fire.
FAANG rank The same chart shows relative rank of the five FAANG stocks. The ranks are determined by the ZYX Change Method , which takes into account not only probability-adjusted rewards but also probability-adjusted risks. Facebook is ranked No. 1, and Netflix is fifth. 
Benefit from some sophistication Most investors can benefit from some of the sophisticated techniques that smart money uses.
The smart money puts lots of emphasis on risk and takes a portfolio approach. With the run in tech stocks, these have become outsize positions in many portfolios. 
From a risk perspective, it doesn’t make sense to add to positions that are already disproportionately large. Instead, it makes sense to trim into strength. 
Doubling your returns Investors can often double their returns by using a simple technique: building a core position and holding it for a very long time, then trading around the core position with positions that have a shorter time horizon, closer stops and closer targets. In some ways, these trade-around positions are similar to swing trading. 
As an example, look at Intel INTC, -0.90% At The Arora Report, Intel was bought at an average price of $34.01 for the long term. Please click here for the annotated chart of Intel; for each successive buy signal shown on the chart, a trade-around position has been started. To learn more, please see “ How to judge Intel stock after the earnings-driven leap .” 
Control your emotions Human nature being what it is, emotions can get in the way of making good investing decisions. A simple antidote is to not make the two mistakes that many investors are making now. Please see “ The average investor is making a classic mistake as the Dow marches to 30,000 ” and “ No FOMO? Don’t make this other classic stock-market investment mistake .”
Read: Mark Hulbert says market timers just gave stock investors a reason to celebrate 
What to do now Investors ought to consider following the smart money as market conditions are beginning to change. Nine of the 10 market-timing categories I look at have turned negative; only the leading economic indicators category is still positive. Most worrisome are valuation vs. competition, and sentiment. Bonds are now offering stronger competition to stocks because of rising interest rates. Sentiment is a contrary indicator when it becomes extremely positive.
The smart money is buying Facebook; it makes sense to buy Facebook on pullbacks in the buy zone.
Read: Facebook earnings lead to praise of ‘powerful’ ad business 
Those not in tech stocks may consider waiting for dips in the buy zones to initiate positions. Buy zones are dynamic and change based on market conditions. They are designed for a 70% probability of a fill over the next 120 days. The point is to buy as low as possible. 
Those in these positions may consider continuing to hold but review to make sure they have not become disproportionately large in the context of a total portfolio. If they have become disproportionately large, it is better to start scaling out in small tranches into strength as opposed to panicking and selling into weakness. It is important to hold on to core positions. These stocks do have considerable upside potential, perhaps after a pull back. 
Those in positions that are properly sized may consider starting new trade-around positions when signals are given.
